hero.headline: Whistleblower alleges DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
hero.teaser: A government plan to mark millions of living people as deceased was part of an immigration enforcement push, according to a whistleblower.
hero.body:
A whistleblower has alleged that a plan developed as part of an immigration enforcement push would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government records.

The whistleblower's claims raise questions about the accuracy of government databases and the potential consequences for individuals who might be incorrectly listed as deceased. Being wrongly marked as dead in federal systems can affect access to benefits, financial accounts, and other services that rely on government records for verification.

cards.headline: US Strikes Iranian Radar Sites After Shooting Down Drones Near Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The US military struck Iranian drone launch sites and radar installations after shooting down Iranian attack drones near the Strait of Hormuz, according to military officials. The strikes targeted coastal sites in Iran following what the US military described as Iranian drones heading toward the strategic waterway, one of the world's most important oil shipping routes.

The US Central Command said the operation was conducted in response to what it characterized as Iranian aggression in the region. The drones were intercepted before reaching the strait, which connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and serves as a transit point for roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption. The military confirmed that radar facilities used to guide the drones were among the sites hit in the retaliatory strikes.

The confrontation marks a significant escalation in tensions between Washington and Tehran. The Strait of Hormuz has long been a flashpoint for conflict, with Iran having previously threatened to close the waterway during periods of heightened tension. Any disruption to shipping through the strait has immediate implications for global energy markets and international trade.

The strikes come as reports indicate ongoing uncertainty surrounding diplomatic talks between the US and Iran. Separate incidents in the region include an Iranian attack on Kuwait airport that resulted in casualties, according to some reports, though those details have not been independently confirmed by US officials. Israel and Lebanon separately agreed to renew a ceasefire, suggesting broader regional efforts to contain spreading conflict.

The Pentagon has not disclosed whether there were casualties from the US strikes on Iranian sites. Iranian officials have not yet issued a formal response to the attacks. The confrontation raises questions about whether the situation will escalate further or whether diplomatic channels can prevent additional military action. US forces maintain a significant presence in the region, including naval assets that patrol the waters around the strait and military bases in neighboring countries.

cards.headline: Putin Rejects Meeting With Zelenskyy to Discuss Ending Ukraine War
cards.teaser: The Russian president said he sees no point in face-to-face talks with his Ukrainian counterpart over ending the conflict.
cards.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected an offer from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to meet for face-to-face peace negotiations. Speaking at the St. Petersburg economic forum, Putin called Zelenskyy's open letter "rude" and said he saw "no point" in such talks, refusing even to use Zelenskyy's name when responding.

Putin reaffirmed Russia's commitment to achieving its war objectives in Ukraine, including seizing the eastern Donbas region. The rejection came as business and political leaders at the forum debated whether Russia should end the conflict or continue bearing its economic and human costs.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Ordering Village Evacuations
cards.teaser: Israeli forces carried out attacks in southern Lebanon after ordering residents of nine villages to evacuate.
cards.body:
Israel launched military strikes in southern Lebanon following evacuation orders for nine villages in the region. The U.S. announced a renewed ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon, though Hezbollah rejected certain terms of the deal.

During the strikes, a United Nations peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon, according to UNIFIL, the U.N. peacekeeping mission in the country.

cards.headline: Xi Jinping to Visit North Korea in Rare Trip Next Week
cards.teaser: The Chinese president will travel to North Korea for his first visit since 2019 to meet with Kim Jong Un.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit North Korea next week for talks with leader Kim Jong Un, his first trip since 2019. Both countries announced the visit on Friday, a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility for producing nuclear fuel.

The timing is significant, coming weeks after Xi met with the leaders of the US and Russia. As North Korea's most important economic and political ally, China plays a crucial role in the country's foreign policy and international relations.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Tumble on Jobs Data and Tech Sell-Off
cards.teaser: US stock markets fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping 695 points as investors reacted to a stronger-than-expected jobs report .
cards.body:
US stock markets fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping 695 points as investors reacted to a stronger-than-expected jobs report and sold technology shares. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite posted their biggest percentage declines since 2025, driven by steep losses in the tech sector. The Nasdaq fell 4 percent, marking its worst single-day performance since April 2025. Treasury yields rose following the employment data.

The jobs report showed strength in the labor market, which raised concerns among traders about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy direction. Stronger employment numbers can signal persistent economic activity that might prompt the Fed to raise interest rates or delay rate cuts. Bond yields climbed as investors priced in higher odds of a Fed rate hike, putting pressure on stock valuations.

Technology stocks bore the brunt of the selloff, with artificial intelligence-related companies and semiconductor manufacturers posting significant declines. Chip stocks led the losses, with shares of Broadcom and Intel falling as part of a broader retreat from the AI trade that had driven much of the market's gains in recent months. The sharp reversal suggests investors are reassessing valuations in the sector after extended gains.

The market downturn reflects growing uncertainty about the economic outlook and Fed policy. Higher interest rates typically pressure stock prices by increasing borrowing costs and making bonds more attractive relative to equities. The tech sector is particularly sensitive to rate changes because many technology companies are valued based on future earnings, which become less valuable when discounted at higher rates.

Friday's decline marks a notable shift in market sentiment. The simultaneous drop in stocks and rise in bond yields indicates investors are repositioning portfolios in response to economic data. Whether the selloff represents a temporary correction or the start of a broader market adjustment will depend on incoming economic indicators and Fed communications in the coming weeks.

cards.headline: Google Agrees to Pay SpaceX Nearly $1 Billion Monthly for Cloud Computing
cards.teaser: Google will pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI, according to a new cloud-computing agreement.
cards.body:
Google has agreed to pay SpaceX approximately $920 million each month for access to computing capacity, according to multiple reports. The deal represents a $30 billion arrangement over its duration and reflects growing demand for the infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence applications.

Under the agreement, Google will gain access to computing resources at data centers operated by xAI, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Elon Musk. A Google representative stated that the deal resulted from unexpected demand for the company's recently launched AI products.

The computing power Google is purchasing will help support the development and operation of large language models and other AI applications. This deal underscores the massive scale of investment required to build and maintain the computational infrastructure that modern AI systems demand.

SpaceX has positioned itself as a major player in the AI computing space. The company recently completed construction of the Colossus data center, which represents a significant capital investment. According to SpaceX's IPO prospectus filed ahead of its anticipated stock market debut, the xAI unit accounted for $12.7 billion of the company's $20.7 billion capital expenditure, primarily due to data center construction costs.

The Google deal follows a similar arrangement SpaceX previously secured with Anthropic for AI compute capacity. These agreements highlight how artificial intelligence companies and major tech firms are increasingly willing to spend enormous sums to access the computing infrastructure necessary for AI development.

SpaceX's xAI unit has become a significant cost center for the company. The AI division lost $6.4 billion last year, driven largely by higher computing expenses needed to build and operate AI models, including Grok, Musk's artificial intelligence tool. However, major contracts like the Google deal suggest SpaceX is working to offset these losses through revenue from other companies seeking computing power.

The timing of the announcement is significant as SpaceX prepares for what is expected to be one of the largest initial public offerings in history. The company is aiming to raise $75 billion through its stock market listing, which is scheduled for early June. The IPO will value SpaceX at approximately $1.77 trillion.

The company's three business segments include space operations, which handles rocket launches for clients including NASA; connectivity, which operates Starlink satellite broadband service; and AI, which encompasses xAI and the X platform formerly known as Twitter. The AI segment generated $3.2 billion in revenue last year, though it remains heavily loss-making. Connectivity was the only segment to turn a profit in the first quarter of 2026.

cards.headline: EU Moves Toward Offering Membership Path for Candidate Countries
cards.teaser: European Union leaders discussed plans to accelerate integration of Western Balkan nations through a new framework.
cards.body:
The European Union advanced plans to create a pathway for candidate countries to begin integration before achieving full membership. Leaders at a Balkans summit expressed optimism about rapid expansion, with German Chancellor and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen participating in discussions about the framework.

Von der Leyen said Montenegro could join the EU by 2028 following the summit. The push to expand comes as the bloc seeks to counter Russian and Chinese influence in the region. The membership framework would allow candidate nations to participate in certain EU programs and structures before completing the full accession process.

cards.headline: France Opens Investigation Into Israeli Treatment of Gaza Flotilla Activists
cards.teaser: French authorities launched an inquiry after activists detained while trying to reach Gaza reported abuse in Israeli custody.
cards.body:
France has launched an investigation into allegations that Israeli authorities mistreated pro-Palestinian activists detained after a flotilla attempted to reach Gaza. The activists claim they were abused while in Israeli custody following their detention.

Israeli authorities have denied the mistreatment allegations. The flotilla was intercepted as it tried to reach Gaza, and its participants were taken into custody.

cards.headline: Astronauts Return to ISS After Sheltering During Russian Repair Attempt
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to their normal stations after a Russian effort to fix an air leak triggered safety protocols.
cards.body:
Two air leaks were discovered in the Zveda module's transfer chamber during a pressurization procedure. Russian specialists detected the leaks while pressurizing the transfer chamber to the ISS. NASA ordered five astronauts aboard the station to prepare for a possible evacuation as a precaution.

The astronauts have now returned to their regular positions after the repair attempt was paused. The incident highlighted the serious protocols in place for addressing air leaks on the orbiting station, where maintaining cabin pressure is critical.

hero.headline: Flesh-Eating Screwworm Detected in Texas for First Time Since 1960s
hero.body:
Federal and state officials confirmed the presence of the New World screwworm in a calf in southern Texas, approximately 50 miles from the Mexico border. This marks the first confirmed detection of the parasitic fly in the state since 1966 and represents a significant concern for the nation's cattle industry at a time when beef prices are at record highs.

The screwworm fly's larvae feed on the blood and flesh of warm-blooded animals like cattle. Female flies target open wounds to lay their eggs, and when the larvae hatch they quickly consume blood and tissue. Without treatment, infected animals will die. While the risk to humans is low, the parasite can spread rapidly in areas with large concentrations of livestock.

The United States successfully eradicated the screwworm in the 1970s after it caused tens of millions of dollars in losses. For more than a year, the USDA and Texas officials have warned ranchers about the parasite's advancement through Mexico, where it has traveled more than 1,100 miles from the south despite ongoing control efforts.

Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller expressed frustration with the USDA's response, stating that despite billions of sterile flies being dispersed, the screwworm still reached Texas. He argued the agency missed an important component of its containment strategy and called for increased deployment of the screwworm adult suppression system, known as Swass, which combines attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins pushed back against concerns, insisting there is no threat of mass infestation and no reason to believe the parasite will become established in the country. She noted the Texas case was the only confirmed case so far.

The USDA has previously relied on releasing sterile male flies to break the breeding cycle, since female screwworm flies mate only once in their months-long lives and do not reproduce with sterile males. In March, Rollins announced the USDA would partner with the Army Corps of Engineers and Mortenson Construction to build a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas.

Past eradication campaigns proved highly successful, leading the US to shut down most sterile fly breeding facilities decades ago, with only one remaining in Panama. In Mexico, high treatment costs have forced some ranchers to use crude measures like applying gasoline or lime to open wounds to remove worms.

The detection has prompted neighboring states to issue alerts and monitor for potential spread across state lines as officials work to assess the scope of the outbreak and prevent the parasite from establishing a permanent presence in the region.

cards.headline: Virginia Man Sentenced to Life for Killing Wife in Plot with Au Pair
cards.teaser: Brendan Banfield received a life sentence for murdering his wife and a stranger during an affair with the family's au pair.
cards.body:
Brendan Banfield, a former IRS law enforcement officer, was sentenced to life in prison without parole for murdering his wife Christine and Joseph Ryan. Banfield claimed he shot Ryan in self-defense after discovering him attacking Christine on February 24, 2023. However, prosecutors proved that Banfield and the family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães, orchestrated the crimes as part of an affair.

The scheme involved luring Ryan to the couple's Virginia home under false pretenses to frame him as the killer. Christine Banfield was a pediatric intensive care nurse. The conviction followed evidence presented by prosecutors detailing the relationship and planning between Banfield and the au pair that led to both deaths.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra Advances to November Runoff in California Governor Race
cards.teaser: The former Health and Human Services Secretary secured the top spot in California's gubernatorial primary with millions of ballots still uncounted.
cards.body:
Democrat Xavier Becerra secured first place in California's gubernatorial primary and will advance to November's general election. The former Health and Human Services Secretary emerged from a crowded primary field in what has been described as a remarkable comeback victory during a turbulent campaign season.

Election officials are still counting millions of ballots to determine Becerra's November opponent. The second-place finisher could be Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who promoted progressive policies including universal healthcare, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality backed by Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Justice Department Argues Courts Cannot Block White House Ballroom Construction
cards.teaser: Federal attorneys contended in appeals court that the president has authority over White House grounds, comparing it to hypothetical authority over other federal landmarks.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is asking a federal appeals court to overturn a lower court decision blocking construction of a $400 million ballroom at the White House. A Department of Justice lawyer argued that no court has authority to halt the project, contending that only Congress possesses the power to stop it. The administration claims presidential control over the White House extends to major alterations on its grounds.

The ballroom would be built on the site of the White House's demolished East Wing. Meanwhile, construction of a secure underground bunker at the location has been permitted to proceed while the legal dispute continues. Washington DC preservationists have challenged the project's scope and approval process.

cards.headline: Senate Candidate Graham Platner Faces New Allegations Days Before Maine Primary
cards.teaser: Multiple women who dated the Democratic Senate candidate described unsettling behavior, drawing concern from supporters ahead of the primary election.
cards.body:
Several women who previously dated Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner described unsettling experiences with him in a New York Times report released days before the state's Democratic primary. The allegations surfaced as Platner pursues the Democratic Senate nomination in a competitive race.

Platner has denied the accusations, characterizing them as physical roughness allegations. He has suggested that the report and other recent controversies indicate his campaign is gaining momentum.

cards.headline: U.S. Military Strikes Iranian Drones and Radar Sites in Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: American forces targeted Iranian military assets that posed a threat to maritime traffic in the strategic waterway.
cards.body:
U.S. Central Command struck Iranian drones and radar installations in and around the Strait of Hormuz. According to U.S. military officials, the drones posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic through the strategic waterway, which serves as a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments.

The military action was a response to what U.S. officials characterized as a direct threat to commercial shipping in the Persian Gulf region.

cards.headline: Sesame Street's Elmo Called Traitor by New Yorkers Over Knicks Finals Stance
cards.teaser: The children's television character faced backlash from New York basketball fans for not fully supporting the city's NBA team.
cards.body:
The Sesame Street character Elmo drew criticism from New Yorkers after failing to fully back the New York Knicks during the NBA finals. The fictional character, whose home is portrayed as being in New York City on the children's program, was labeled a traitor by fans upset over his response to the basketball championship series.

The incident highlights the intensity of sports fandom in New York during the Knicks' finals appearance. Elmo has been a fixture on Sesame Street for decades and is commonly associated with New York City through the show's setting.

cards.headline: States Prepare Antitrust Lawsuit to Block Paramount-Warner Bros Merger
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are preparing legal action to prevent Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros on antitrust grounds, according to sources familiar with the matter.
cards.body:
US states are readying a lawsuit to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, citing antitrust concerns about the merger's impact on competition. At least 10 states are considering joining the legal challenge, with California expected to announce a decision soon on whether it will participate in efforts to stop the deal. The states argue the merger would harm consumers and reduce competition in the entertainment industry.

Paramount has asked a judge to dismiss a separate consumer antitrust lawsuit seeking to block the merger. A lawyer for Paramount claimed that opponents of the Warner Bros deal hold antisemitic views, according to reports. The legal battles represent significant obstacles to completing the acquisition.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Considers Taking Equity Stakes in AI Companies
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump said the US government may take equity positions in artificial intelligence firms as part of potential partnerships between the administration and AI companies.
cards.body:
President Trump has indicated the U.S. government is exploring acquiring equity stakes in artificial intelligence companies. The administration plans to hold meetings with AI firms, including OpenAI, to discuss potential government partnerships and profit-sharing arrangements.

This approach would represent a significant shift in U.S. industrial policy, moving away from traditional hands-off market practices toward direct government ownership in private technology companies.

cards.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 Amid Jobs Data and Market Pressure
cards.teaser: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 to its lowest level since October 2024 as the strong jobs report and a bug in Zcash added pressure to cryptocurrency markets.
cards.body:
Bitcoin dropped to $60,000, its lowest level since October 2024, as broader market turmoil intensified following the release of U.S. jobs data. The U.S. added 172,000 jobs in May while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3%, but wage gains slowed. The stronger-than-expected employment figures triggered a sharp market selloff.

Major stock indices fell sharply on June 5, with the Nasdaq closing down 4%—its largest single-day drop in over a year—following significant losses in technology and AI chip stocks. The S&P 500 dropped 2.6% and the Dow fell 695 points. Cryptocurrency markets faced additional pressure from a bug affecting Zcash.

cards.headline: Advanced Nuclear Reactor Reaches Critical Milestone
cards.teaser: An advanced nuclear reactor has become the first to reach a critical milestone, according to the US Department of Energy.
cards.body:
The Department of Energy announced that an advanced nuclear reactor has achieved a significant development milestone, marking the first such accomplishment for this type of reactor technology. The agency characterized the achievement as critical for the advancement of nuclear energy in the United States.

The milestone represents progress in efforts to develop next-generation nuclear power technology. Advanced reactors are designed to offer improved safety features and efficiency compared to traditional nuclear power plants.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Tops List of Highest-Paid CEOs
cards.teaser: Executive compensation is rising while worker pay growth lags, widening the gap between CEO pay and rank-and-file employees in corporate America.
cards.body:
Elon Musk leads the list of highest-paid chief executive officers as executive compensation continues to accelerate. The gap between CEO pay and compensation for ordinary workers is expanding, according to new data on corporate pay practices.

Executive pay packages have grown at a faster rate than wages for rank-and-file employees, continuing a trend of increasing inequality within companies. The disparity reflects broader patterns in corporate compensation structures across American businesses.

hero.headline: Bluetooth Speakers Can Hack PCs Remotely Through USB Connection, Researchers Find
hero.body:
Security researchers have discovered a critical vulnerability that allows hackers to compromise Windows computers through certain USB-connected speakers without any user interaction. The exploit, called Pwnd Blaster, targets Creative's Sound Blaster Katana V2X speaker system, which retails for approximately $300.

The attack works by exploiting the Bluetooth functionality built into the speaker when it is connected to a PC via USB. Researchers demonstrated that an attacker within Bluetooth range can send malicious commands through the speaker to the connected computer, gaining unauthorized access without the user touching the device or clicking anything. The vulnerability represents a new attack vector because it bypasses traditional security measures that rely on detecting suspicious user behavior.

Creative, the manufacturer of the affected speaker, does not consider the behavior a security vulnerability. The company has not indicated whether it plans to release a firmware update or other fix to address the issue. This stance has drawn criticism from security professionals who argue that any device capable of compromising a computer without user consent represents a significant security risk.

The discovery has prompted concern among PC users about the security implications of connected peripherals. Security experts recommend that users consider disconnecting USB microphones and speakers when not in use, particularly in environments where sensitive data is handled. The attack highlights how peripheral devices with wireless capabilities can create unexpected security holes in otherwise protected systems.

The Pwnd Blaster exploit adds to growing concerns about the security of Internet of Things devices and connected peripherals. As more consumer electronics incorporate wireless connectivity and direct system access through USB connections, the potential attack surface for malicious actors continues to expand. Security researchers continue to investigate whether similar vulnerabilities exist in other USB-connected audio devices from different manufacturers.

cards.headline: Five Astronauts Shelter on Space Station During Russian Air Leak Repair
cards.teaser: Astronauts moved to a safe area aboard the International Space Station while Russian crew members attempted to fix an air leak.
cards.body:
Two air leaks were discovered in the Zvezda module's transfer chamber during pressurization procedures. Russian specialists detected the leaks while preparing the chamber, prompting NASA to order five astronauts aboard the International Space Station into their docked Crew Dragon spacecraft and spacesuits as a precaution against potential emergency evacuation.

The crew, including two US astronauts, a French astronaut, and a Russian cosmonaut from NASA's Crew-12 mission, received evacuation orders at 9:04 a.m. ET on Friday. After the repair attempt was paused, NASA cleared the astronauts to return to normal station duties.

cards.headline: Reid Hoffman Steps Down From Microsoft Board to Focus on AI Drug Discovery Startup
cards.teaser: LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman is leaving Microsoft's board of directors after a decade to concentrate on his artificial intelligence company.
cards.body:
Reid Hoffman is stepping down from Microsoft's board after a decade of service to focus on Manus, his artificial intelligence drug discovery startup. During his tenure at Microsoft, Hoffman benefited significantly from the company's substantial growth in market value.

Hoffman's move represents a shift to "founder mode" as he dedicates himself to building Manus, which applies AI technology to pharmaceutical research and drug development. His departure marks the end of his involvement with one of the world's largest technology companies.

cards.headline: Square Enix Announces Final Fantasy VII Revelation for Spring 2027 Release
cards.teaser: The third and final installment of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy will launch simultaneously across all platforms in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix officially unveiled Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final installment in its remake trilogy. The game will launch simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027. The announcement was made at Summer Game Fest Live and included footage showcasing the game.

Revelation will conclude the story that began with the 2020 Final Fantasy VII Remake and continued in its sequel, bringing the company's multi-game reimagining of the 1997 original to a close.

cards.headline: Shift Up Announces Stellar Blade: Blood Rain Sequel
cards.teaser: The developer behind Stellar Blade has announced a sequel titled Stellar Blade: Blood Rain, currently in development.
cards.body:
Shift Up has announced Stellar Blade: Blood Rain, a sequel to its action game Stellar Blade. The developer revealed the game through a debut trailer that showcases a darker, more horror-focused direction compared to the original title.

The game retains character design elements from the first installment. Shift Up is currently developing the sequel, with the announcement made during a major gaming presentation where multiple other sequels and new titles were also revealed.

cards.headline: Capcom to Release Resident Evil: Veronica Remake in 2027
cards.teaser: Capcom announced a remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica, retitled simply as Resident Evil Veronica, set for release next year.
cards.body:
Capcom revealed Resident Evil Veronica, a remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica, scheduled to launch in 2027. The game drops 'Code' from the original title and will be released for multiple platforms including Nintendo Switch 2. The announcement continues Capcom's strategy of remaking classic entries in the survival horror franchise.

Resident Evil: Code Veronica originally released in 2000 and is considered an important entry in the series' history. The remake follows successful remakes of Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 3, and Resident Evil 4, which updated classic games with modern graphics and gameplay mechanics.

cards.headline: ArenaNet Announces Guild Wars 3 for PC and PlayStation 5
cards.teaser: The third installment in the Guild Wars franchise was announced with a beta planned for next year.
cards.body:
ArenaNet announced Guild Wars 3 during Summer Game Fest, with the game coming to PC and PlayStation 5. A beta test is scheduled for next year, giving players an early look at the new entry in the online role-playing game series. The developer described the game as a modern evolution of the multiplayer online role-playing game genre.

Guild Wars 3 is set 1,000 years before the events of the original Guild Wars game. The announcement raises questions about the future of Guild Wars 2, which continues to operate with an active player base. ArenaNet has not provided details on how the two games will coexist or whether Guild Wars 2 will continue receiving updates.

hero.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead over Spurs in NBA Finals
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 1 of the NBA Finals, winning 105-95 on the road to move one step closer to their first championship since 1973. The victory extended New York's remarkable playoff streak and set up a crucial Game 2 matchup in San Antonio.

The Knicks arrived at the Finals riding an 11-game winning streak, but faced a formidable challenge against the Spurs and their star player Victor Wembanyama. Despite falling behind by 14 points in the third quarter, New York showcased the resilience that has defined their playoff run. The team, which previously overcame a 22-point deficit against the Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals, mounted another comeback to seize control of the game.

Jalen Brunson led the Knicks' fourth-quarter surge, scoring 13 of his game-high 30 points in the final period. His ability to deliver in clutch moments has been central to New York's postseason success. OG Anunoby contributed significantly as well, scoring 12 of his 17 points in the fourth quarter. The Knicks proved particularly sharp down the stretch, committing zero turnovers in the fourth quarter while outscoring the Spurs with an 11-0 run to close out the game.

Wembanyama finished with 26 points, 12 rebounds and three blocks for San Antonio, but fell short of his usual dominant performance. The young star shot just 6-of-21 from the field and briefly left the court with an injury in the third quarter before returning. After the game, Wembanyama took responsibility for his struggles, saying "I was bad tonight, it's not more complicated than that." He added that nerves were not a factor in the Spurs' performance, despite the magnitude of the Finals occasion.

San Antonio struggled down the stretch, committing five turnovers in the fourth quarter while shooting just 28.6 percent. The home crowd proved unable to spur a comeback as the Spurs wilted in the final minutes.

Brunson also dealt with injury concerns during the contest. He collided with San Antonio's Harrison Barnes at the end of the first quarter and suffered a knee injury, forcing him to briefly leave the game. He returned in the second quarter but appeared to injure his ankle on a subsequent layup, though he remained in the game.

Game 2 is scheduled for Friday night in San Antonio before the best-of-seven series moves to Madison Square Garden for what promises to be an energetic Game 3 on Monday. The Knicks are now one victory away from taking a commanding 3-0 series advantage, while the Spurs must find a way to rebound at home.

cards.headline: NASCAR Hall of Famer Ned Jarrett dies at 93
cards.teaser: The two-time Cup champion and longtime broadcaster died of natural causes at his North Carolina home.
cards.body:
NASCAR Hall of Famer Ned Jarrett died Thursday at his home in Newton, North Carolina, according to his family. He was 93 and passed away peacefully of natural causes.

Jarrett was a two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion whose influence on motorsports extended well beyond his racing career. He became a prominent broadcaster who helped bring NASCAR to wider audiences across the country.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses World Cup water bottle ban after backlash
cards.teaser: The organization will now allow fans to bring refillable water bottles into tournament stadiums across North America.
cards.body:
FIFA has reversed its decision to prohibit World Cup fans from bringing refillable water bottles into the tournament's 16 stadiums across North America. The policy change follows significant public backlash against the original ban.

Attendees can now carry water bottles into venues during the World Cup. The reversal came after the initial ban drew fierce criticism from fans and officials concerned about the restriction.

cards.headline: Messi could play World Cup warmups as hamstring improves
cards.teaser: The Argentina star is recovering from muscle fatigue and may see minutes before the team's tournament opener.
cards.body:
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni reported that Lionel Messi is recovering well from muscle fatigue affecting his left hamstring. The captain could see action in warmup matches leading up to Argentina's World Cup debut on June 16.

Messi's fitness has been a crucial question for Argentina as they aim to defend their World Cup title. The warmup games will provide an opportunity for the veteran to build match sharpness before the tournament begins.

cards.headline: NBA interviews Kawhi Leonard in Clippers salary cap probe
cards.teaser: League investigators spoke with the star and his business adviser about allegations the team violated compensation rules.
cards.body:
LA Clippers star Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser have been interviewed by NBA investigators as part of the league's ongoing probe into the team's compensation practices.

The investigation centers on whether the Clippers provided Leonard with additional compensation outside the team's official salary structure, which would violate NBA rules designed to maintain competitive balance across the league.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge says rib injury stems from April dive
cards.teaser: The Yankees outfielder traced the stress fracture in his right rib to a defensive play in late April.
cards.body:
Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has traced his right rib stress fracture to a diving play in late April. The injury has sidelined the slugger during a crucial stretch of the season.

Judge pinpointed the exact moment the fracture occurred, revealing how the defensive effort led to the ongoing issue affecting his availability.

cards.headline: Iran players receive US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: The team will be able to enter and compete in the tournament hosted across North America.
cards.body:
A U.S. official confirmed to ABC News that Iran's World Cup team players have received visas permitting them to enter and compete in the United States. The approval allows Iran to move forward with participating in the tournament being held across North America.

The visa clearance had drawn significant attention due to the historically tense diplomatic relations between the two countries. With the visas now granted, Iran can complete their final World Cup preparations ahead of the competition.

hero.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
hero.body:
British actor Anthony Head, best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head gained prominence for his role as the mentor and school librarian in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, serving as a father figure to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character throughout the show's seven-season run. His portrayal made him recognizable to audiences worldwide. More recently, he appeared in the comedy series Ted Lasso, where he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion and received praise for his on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

His television career extended across multiple genres and decades. He took a recurring role in the BBC sketch show Little Britain, appearing as a British prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant played by David Walliams. He also appeared in the BBC production of Merlin. Beyond television, Head featured in films including The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie.

Before achieving international fame, Head established himself on the British stage. He starred in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell and later took the lead role as Freddie Trumper in the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988. He also performed as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

In the 1980s, Head sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and was featured on their 1986 debut album The Circle and the Square. He became widely recognized in the UK and US for his appearances in Nescafé Gold Blend television advertisements, which depicted the slow-burn courtship between a British couple.

Head was born in Camden, London, and raised by artistic parents. His father was a documentary filmmaker who founded Verity Films, while his mother was an actor who played Madame Maigret in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also pursued an acting career.

When filming Buffy the Vampire Slayer required him to move to Los Angeles, Head maintained his commitment to his family in England. He arranged his work schedule to return home every three or four weeks, spending considerable money on airfares to see his partner Sarah and two young daughters.

Sarah Fisher, Head's partner, died in December 2025 at age 61. His daughters noted that his legacy will continue through the shows he appeared in and the audiences who cherish them.

cards.headline: Man Charged with Murder of Veteran Character Actor James Handy
cards.teaser: A man has been charged with murder in the stabbing death of veteran character actor James Handy at a home in Tarzana, California.
cards.body:
Veteran character actor James Handy, 81, was found stabbed in the chest outside his Los Angeles home on Wednesday and later died from his injuries. Michael Gledhill, 44, was charged with murder in connection with the killing. Gledhill is the son of Handy's girlfriend.

Handy had a long career in film and television, including roles in Jumanji and Top Gun: Maverick.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Releases Toy Story Music Video
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift released a music video featuring the character Jessie from the Toy Story films.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift released a new music video for "I Knew It," a song written for Toy Story's cowgirl character Jessie. The video takes a nostalgic approach to the beloved animated character.

Swift acknowledged the challenge of following Randy Newman's iconic Toy Story soundtrack work, calling him "incomparable" and crediting him with creating the musical world of the films. The song showcases Swift's country roots and has been praised for its craftsmanship and emotional resonance with viewers.

cards.headline: Reports Claim Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Planning July Wedding
cards.teaser: Multiple reports suggest Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are planning a July wedding at Madison Square Garden in New York City.
cards.body:
Reports circulating in entertainment media suggest Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce may wed in July at Madison Square Garden. The reports claim over 1,000 people have been invited to the event. The NYPD commissioner made a joke about the rumored wedding during public remarks.

The reports remain unconfirmed speculation, with fans and media outlets discussing the potential timing and venue. Madison Square Garden would represent an unconventional but high-profile location for a celebrity wedding of this magnitude.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with 2027 Release
cards.teaser: Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final game in its remake trilogy, set for spring 2027 release.
cards.body:
Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final game in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy. The game will release in spring 2027 across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. A trailer for the title was shown at Summer Game Fest Live.

The release will complete Square Enix's multi-year project to reimagine the original Final Fantasy VII across three separate games.

cards.headline: Among Us Animated Series Debuts on Paramount Plus
cards.teaser: All 10 episodes of an animated Among Us television series dropped on Paramount Plus without prior announcement.
cards.body:
An animated television series based on the video game Among Us became available on Paramount Plus. All 10 episodes of the series were released simultaneously. Stars Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson announced the surprise release at Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles.

The announcement caught audiences off guard, as the series had not been promoted ahead of its release. The show adapts the popular multiplayer game into an animated format for streaming audiences.

cards.headline: Legendary Rock Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: Greg James, a tattoo artist known for his work with rock musicians, has died at age 71.
cards.body:
Greg James, a tattoo artist who worked extensively with rock music figures, died at age 71. James became known in the music industry for his tattoo work with prominent musicians and bands over several decades.

James built a reputation as a go-to artist within rock music circles. His death was reported by TMZ, though specific details about the cause were not provided in initial reports.

hero.headline: Whistleblower alleges DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
hero.teaser: A government plan to mark millions of living people as deceased was part of an immigration enforcement push, according to a whistleblower.
hero.body:
A whistleblower has alleged that a plan developed as part of an immigration enforcement push would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government records.

The whistleblower's claims raise questions about the accuracy of government databases and the potential consequences for individuals who might be incorrectly listed as deceased. Being wrongly marked as dead in federal systems can affect access to benefits, financial accounts, and other services that rely on government records for verification.

cards.headline: U.S. military shoots down Iranian drones, strikes radar sites in Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: The U.S.
cards.body:
The U.S. military intercepted four Iranian drones heading toward the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to Central Command. The drones posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic in the strategic waterway. In response, U.S. forces struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites in Goruk, located in Hormozgan province, and on Qeshm Island.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical passage for global oil shipments, with roughly one-fifth of the world's petroleum traveling through the narrow waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. The U.S. Navy regularly operates in the region to protect commercial vessels and maintain freedom of navigation.

cards.headline: Justice Department says anti-weaponization fund will not continue
cards.teaser: The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund is effectively dead, the DOJ told a federal court.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" compensation fund will not continue, the Justice Department announced in a court filing Friday. Two DOJ attorneys informed a federal court in Virginia of the decision while requesting dismissal of a legal challenge brought by a former federal prosecutor and others.

The fund was created to compensate individuals for what the administration described as weaponization of government agencies. The announcement came as the case proceeds in the Eastern District of Virginia.

cards.headline: Chief of staff for Texas congressman faces firearm charges after Capitol incident
cards.teaser: Luis Vega, chief of staff for Rep. Pete Sessions, was charged with two counts related to allegedly attempting to bring a firearm into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, the chief of staff for Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas, is facing firearm charges months after he allegedly attempted to bring a gun into the U.S. Capitol complex. Vega was charged Wednesday with two counts in connection with the alleged incident that occurred days before Christmas last year.

The charges come several months after the initial alleged incident took place. Sessions is a Republican member of the House of Representatives from Texas. The specific nature of the two charges filed against Vega and the current status of his employment with the congressman were not detailed in the available information.

cards.headline: Trump visits Wisconsin farmers amid rising agricultural costs
cards.teaser: The president traveled to Wisconsin to address farmers dealing with higher fertilizer and fuel prices.
cards.body:
President Trump visited Wisconsin on Friday to speak with farmers facing increased costs for fertilizer and fuel. The trip was billed as an effort to reassure agricultural producers who have been squeezed by surging input prices. During his remarks, Trump also discussed his border policies at length.

The president also spent a portion of his speech talking about fountains in Washington, D.C. The visit comes as farmers across the country deal with elevated costs for key inputs needed to plant and harvest crops. Wisconsin is a major agricultural state with significant dairy and crop production.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth brings six children to France on official trip
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth is covering his family's travel expenses, though officials warned the arrangement could strain his security team.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth brought six of his children to France on an official trip, according to the Pentagon. The Pentagon stated that Hegseth is personally covering his family's travel expenses for the journey, though the decision to bring them along has raised concerns among officials.

Security officials warned that bringing family members on the trip could strain Hegseth's security team during a time of increased threats. The nature of the official business that brought Hegseth to France and the duration of the trip were not specified in available information.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The former Secretary of the Interior under President Biden previously served in the U.S. House of Representatives representing New Mexico.

If elected in November, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.
